art_direction: Native 28px material planes and recognizable connected weapon structure

jobs.prompt:
Create ONE square inventory weapon sprite, redesigned for an actual 24x24-pixel art area in the 2000s Korean 3D MMORPG LAQIA. The first attached tiny native item icon is the authoritative guide for scale, composition, and material shading. The second reference is ONLY the identity of the new weapon to depict. Do not just crop the concept artwork. Art-direct a readable item sprite: contiguous broad metal surfaces, restrained cool highlights, rich dark steel shadow, blue enamel accents, minimal simplified gold fittings. Closely match the original game's softly antialiased prerendered item sprite aesthetic, NOT a glossy macro illustration, NOT jewelry advertising, NOT flat cartoon or chunky retro 8-bit art. Use a pure black background and no frame, text, aura, sparkles, shadow outside the silhouette, or scenery. Produce a square image with the art laid out for eventual reduction to 24 pixels. At that scale the weapon category must be immediately recognizable. Fine micro-engraving, chains and tiny stars should be omitted. Broad structural form is primary, moon ornament is secondary. Crop portions naturally at the square edges just as the native sprite does, retaining meaningful connected weapon parts. No complete miniature weapon floating with margins.
SUBJECT: the blue-moon S-curve greatsword in reference 2, shown in the SAME viewing direction and diagonal framing as the original Black Knight greatsword in reference 1. The substantial curved blade extends OUT the BOTTOM-LEFT corner; the thinner blue grip extends OUT the TOP-RIGHT. Hilt/guard is above center, approximately 65% across and 30% down. Show a LONG clear stretch of BROAD sword blade along the lower-left half, enough to read the flowing S blade. One continuous pale silver-blue cutting plane contrasts against the dark cobalt blade core. The guard is modest and clearly transverse to the blade: a SMALL open crescent on one side and one restrained flowing quillon on the other, identifiable from reference 2 but not an enormous circular ornament. Blade face should occupy about 6-8 of the logical 24 pixels in width; guard no more than about 10 pixels across. Blue gem is only one small glint. Overall metal object occupies roughly 40-45% of the black square. Prioritize a convincingly three-dimensional sword, blade volume, dark hilt, coherent lighting from upper-left. The blade is dominant, never a giant crescent brooch.

The bow must read as a curved tensioned BOW, not staff, dagger, hook or medallion. A fine straight silver-blue bowstring, diagonal at the right side of the curved limb, is unmistakably visible with a generous clean BLACK GAP between string and limb. Bow limb approximately 3-4 logical pixels thick, silver-metal face and dark blue enamel side with understated warm gold connection near grip. Include ONE small crescent silhouette nested into the curve just above the grip, recognizably derived from reference 2, but simplify it to a small accent roughly 3-4 logical pixels wide. Keep 65% of the square pure black negative space, including the open area between bow and string. Silver edge and deep blue core must read clearly in a tiny inventory slot.

The smooth SMALL bright ice-blue moon at the head is only about 4-5 logical pixels across, encircled loosely by the asymmetric blue crescent hook with clearly open black gaps and one sweeping point; do not fill most of the icon with a glowing circular orb. A connected sturdy blue-and-gold SHAFT, about 3 logical pixels thick, runs diagonally for at least 11 logical pixels from that head all the way to and OUT the BOTTOM-LEFT corner.
